points.description: Names the three service classes: unconfirmed connectionless, confirmed connectionless, connection-oriented (any reasonable wording).
points.partial_credit: Two of the three named, or names given without clear distinction: about half.

points.description: Explains the connectionless classes' difference: unconfirmed has no acknowledgement so data can be lost; confirmed uses acknowledgements (with timeout/retransmit) so data is not lost.
points.partial_credit: Mentions only ACK vs no ACK, or only loss vs no loss: about half.

points.description: Explains that connection-oriented differs by having connect/data transfer/disconnect phases, with flow control and reliable, ordered delivery without duplicates, unlike the connectionless classes.
points.partial_credit: Gives only one of: connection setup/release, or reliability/flow control: about half.

rubric.notes: Full marks for naming all three classes and giving the main difference for each: ACK or not, loss or not, and connection phases with flow control. Part marks for vague or incomplete differences, or for naming only some classes. No marks for wrong or missing classes with no relevant differences. Extra minor detail, such as duplicates in the confirmed class, is not needed.
